Question
========
What does Kalecki's phrase "workers spend what they get and capitalists get what they spend" imply?

Answerlist
----------
* The distribution between wages and profits shapes demand, investment, and macroeconomic stability
* Workers save more than capitalists
* Distribution has no effect on the economy as a whole
* Wages are always paid according to marginal productivity

Solution
========
Because workers spend most of their income, a higher wage share supports demand. Profits that are not reinvested weaken demand. Distribution is a macroeconomic question.

Answerlist
----------
* True
* False
* False
* False
